samples.summary: cli.md still asserts the CLI merely re-exports the shared `seg()`, which this change makes false
samples.evidence: § (line 1655-1660) reads: "it carries the same primitive — literally the same one: `seg()` lives in `@wafflebase/core/url` ... and both `packages/cli/src/client/url.ts` and `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` re-export it from there rather than keeping a second copy that can drift." After this diff `packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:31` defines its own `seg()` wrapping `coreSeg` with an extra, CLI-only empty-segment rejection, so the CLI's `seg()` is no longer "literally the same one". The change updates §8.2 and the file-tree entry but leaves this section (the canonical write-up of the primitive) describing the previous architecture, i.e. the design doc now contradicts itself about a security primitive. The nested-doc/backtick CI check cannot catch a prose contradiction.

samples.summary: The cells URL is hand-duplicated in two command files instead of sharing a builder, contradicting this change's own "one definition of the request" principle
samples.evidence: The stated design rationale for `apiKeysUrl()` is that "'the preview is the request' only holds while there is a single definition of the request" (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:77). Yet the new previews rebuild the cells path by hand: cells.ts:30-35 re-implements the three-way endpoint selection and `?range=${encodeURIComponent(range)}`, and sheets-export.ts:52-59 re-implements the same query encoding — both copies of `HttpClient.getCells`/`getCell` (http-client.ts:366-378). The abstraction that was introduced for api-keys (a shared builder in client/url.ts, e.g. `cellsUrlPath(docId, tabId, range)`) was not applied where the drift risk is highest, so the very invariant the change documents is only half enforced.

samples.summary: New CLI-local `seg()` shadows the shared core primitive with a stricter rule — possible wrong-layer placement
samples.evidence: `packages/core/src/url/index.ts:50-53` states the rule lives there "because both build such URLs ... and a rule enforced by two copies is a rule that drifts", and frontend.md:466 calls the frontend module "not a parallel one". The empty-segment hole being closed is a property of the *server's* routing (Express strict routing off), which the browser client hits with the same collection/item routes and the same `useParams`-sourced ids (`packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:49,185`, `share-links.ts:61`) — react-router can yield `''` for a route param just as argv can. If the hole is real, the rule arguably belongs in `@wafflebase/core/url` (optionally parameterised) rather than as a same-named CLI function that a future reader can easily mistake for the shared one.

samples.summary: Unrelated concerns bundled: DNS-rebinding `Host` check and two CI-script fixes ride along with a dry-run/URL-builder change
samples.evidence: The change's subject is `--dry-run` coverage for read commands plus shared URL builders. It also adds a login-callback `Host`/DNS-rebinding guard (login.ts:436-455, plus docs/design/cli.md:227 and the rest-api.md threat-table row) and two unrelated CI/infra fixes (scripts/verify-self.mjs adding `needs: ["core:build"]` to the design-sandbox lane; scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs pinning the push-to-main fall-through). Each is defensible on its own and each is documented, but they are independent changes whose review and revert are now coupled to the dry-run work.

samples.summary: New §8.2 claim "the one command the flag does not hold back is `login`" is inaccurate for local-state mutations
samples.evidence: `logout` (packages/cli/src/commands/logout.ts:8-11) calls `clearSession()` unconditionally, and `ctx switch` (packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:104-106) writes `activeWorkspace` unconditionally — neither consults `opts.dryRun`. Both destroy/mutate on-disk state under `--dry-run`, so `login` is not the only exception. Either the sentence should name them (they issue no HTTP request, which may be the intended reading) or the flag should hold them back too.

samples.summary: Dry-run branch placement is inconsistent with the "a dry run validates inputs" rule the change asserts
samples.evidence: cli.md:1247 says `--dry-run` "validates inputs", and this change deliberately moves validation ahead of the branch in `docs list` (docs.ts:80-86), `files list` (files.ts:87-98) and `sheets export` (sheets-export.ts:47). But the branches added for `docs get` (docs.ts:132), `files get` (files.ts:121 is inside try, after fmt — fine) `sheets tabs list` (tabs.ts:20) and `sheets cells get` (cells.ts:26) run before any `parseOutputFormat`, so `--dry-run --format bogus` previews instead of erroring in some namespaces and errors in others. Same asymmetry in the error surface: a refused id in `docs get` escapes the try/catch and surfaces as a raw throw (the new test asserts `rejects.toThrow`), while `api-keys revoke ..` is enveloped by `outputError` — two different failure shapes for the same refusal, for a CLI whose stated goal is machine-readable output.

The local helper adds a name and a doc comment but no behaviour over calling `apiKeysUrl(getConfig(opts), keyId)` at the three call sites; the rationale it carries would read just as well on the import.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. docs/design/cli.md:1655-1660 states verbatim that "it carries the same primitive — literally the same one: `seg()` lives in `@wafflebase/core/url` ... and both `packages/cli/src/client/url.ts` and `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` re-export it from there rather than keeping a second copy that can drift." That is now false: packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:31-40 defines its own `seg()` that wraps `coreSeg` and adds a CLI-only empty-segment rejection (its own comment at lines 12-19 says "Wrapped rather than re-exported because this package needs one rule more"). Only the frontend half remains accurate (packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts:15 is a bare re-export). The doc also contradicts itself internally: §8.2 at docs/design/cli.md:1293-1301 documents the CLI-only empty-identifier rejection and the `workspaceSeg()` exception, behavior that exists only in the CLI wrapper. So the canonical write-up of a URL-safety/security primitive describes the superseded architecture while another section describes the new one. This is design-doc discipline (canonical subsystem doc not correctly updated for an architecture change), squarely in this lens, and not refutable as not-present, already-guarded, or a taste nit.

finding.summary: The cells URL is hand-duplicated in two command files instead of sharing a builder, contradicting this change's own "one definition of the request" principle
finding.evidence: The stated design rationale for `apiKeysUrl()` is that "'the preview is the request' only holds while there is a single definition of the request" (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:77). Yet the new previews rebuild the cells path by hand: cells.ts:30-35 re-implements the three-way endpoint selection and `?range=${encodeURIComponent(range)}`, and sheets-export.ts:52-59 re-implements the same query encoding — both copies of `HttpClient.getCells`/`getCell` (http-client.ts:366-378). The abstraction that was introduced for api-keys (a shared builder in client/url.ts, e.g. `cellsUrlPath(docId, tabId, range)`) was not applied where the drift risk is highest, so the very invariant the change documents is only half enforced.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is real (cells.ts:30-35, sheets-export.ts:54-60 mirror http-client.ts:366-378), but it is not a blocking design-fit violation. (a) Inline path interpolation is the documented contract for previews: dry-run.ts:4-21 specifies that `path` is relative to the v1 base and identifiers are interpolated with `seg()`, with the base coming from the same `apiV1Base()` builder HttpClient uses — and both cells.ts:10 and sheets-export.ts:7 import and use that shared `seg()`. So the invariants the repo actually documents (one `seg()`, one base builder) ARE enforced here. (b) `apiKeysUrl()` is explicitly scoped as a special case, not a general rule: url.ts:73-79 and dry-run.ts:32-37 both state the api-keys routes sit outside `/api/v1` and therefore "cannot be expressed as a `printDryRun` path"; docs/design/cli.md:1271-1286 states the same scoping and requires sharing only for that route and for `seg()`. No acceptance criterion asks for a `cellsUrlPath()`. (c) No existing module is reinvented — client/url.ts exports only seg, workspaceSeg, apiV1Base, apiKeysUrl (lines 31/64/69/80), so the rubric's `major` bar ("duplicates an existing module") is not met. (d) The identical inline pattern is pre-existing and pervasive (tabs.ts:21,58,90; notes.ts:93,110,131,163; files.ts:65,122,139,162; sheets-import.ts:117), so extracting a builder for cells alone is a DRY/taste preference = `minor`, which never blocks under this lens. The two previews also currently match the client exactly, so no drift exists today.

finding.summary: Single-use `/start` is at odds with the documented headless copy-paste path it is supposed to preserve
finding.evidence: cli.md:176-178 now says step 3 "Opens (and prints, for copy-paste in headless environments) the nonce-free http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start", and cli.md:206-211 claims "the URL a headless user copies is the same one `open()` is given and the same one that works". Those two properties cannot both hold with a one-shot route: `login` always calls `open(startUrl)` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:72) and only falls into the `catch` when the dynamic import or spawn itself throws — `open()` resolves normally in headless/CI environments where a launcher binary exists (xdg-open, `start`, wslview) but no browser ever renders, and browsers can also issue more than one request to a URL (prefetch/preconnect, restored tab). In those cases the first `GET /start` consumes the nonce and the URL the CLI just told the user to visit ("If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.", login.ts:68) answers `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, leaving the invocation with no way to complete — a regression against the prior behaviour, which printed a URL that still worked when the browser did not appear. The design doc asserts the property rather than reconciling it (e.g. allowing re-issue until the callback arrives, or only arming single-use after a successful open).

verdict.reason: The finding's cited artifacts do not exist. docs/design/cli.md:185-187 (step 3) documents opening/printing the backend OAuth URL `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>&nonce=<nonce>&challenge=<...>` — a nonce-carrying URL, not a "nonce-free http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start"; cli.md:207-212 says the loopback listener "accepts only GET /callback" and makes no "same URL" assertion. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:70-73 is the `--allow-unbound-callback` option declaration, not `open(startUrl)`; the sole open is `await deps.openBrowser(oauthUrl)` (login.ts:273) using the identical string printed at login.ts:263. The loopback server (login.ts:543-555) handles only `/callback` and returns a plain 404 for any other path — there is no `/start` route, no nonce consumption on GET, and no `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`; repo-wide grep for `START_CONSUMED`/`startUrl`/`/start` yields no hits in packages/cli or docs/design/cli.md. The only single-use element is the backend confirm secret (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:96-104), and a repeat visit to the printed URL simply re-mints a secret and re-renders the confirm page (lines 106-113), so the printed URL stays usable. Ground: not-present.
